notes: Alignment noise propagates into M5 and M6: an unaligned target sentence may be an elaboration or an alignment failure, and an unaligned source sentence may be deleted or mis-aligned. This is why tau is swept.

params.matching: greedy many-to-many: link(i,j) iff cos(i,j) >= tau

notes: Deletion defined at primary tau=0.5. Alignment noise at this tau propagates into the deleted/retained split.

params.note: No regression or fitted model; effect sizes are the answer.
params.why: cohens_d_deleted_vs_retained pools sentences across documents, which lets document length into the comparison -- textrank is a per-document stationary distribution and correlates with its own document's sentence count at rho=-0.92. stratified_effect computes the deleted-vs-retained difference inside each document and averages those, so a document that cannot support the comparison for a feature is absent from it rather than diluting it.

notes: Automatic elaboration rate is an upper bound on real elaboration until the manual sample is annotated; entailment models degrade off-domain.

Compression distribution is more consistent with two or more modes than one (Sarle's bimodality coefficient=0.619, above 0.555); a mixed corpus has no representative mean compression. Inspect the compression histogram.
Deltas are target - source. The paper this feature set comes from computes complex - simplified, so every delta here has the opposite sign to the corresponding column in its tables.

Self-contained by design: syllables_ratio, sentences_number and the two flesch_* fields duplicate values published by M1/M3a, and lexical_richness, infrequent_words_ratio, syntactic_tree_depth, passive_voice_ratio and words_per_sentence are near-neighbours of existing measures with different definitions. Do not treat all 33 as independent signals.

params.delta_convention: target - source (the paper uses complex - simplified)
deviations_from_paper: flesch_* via readability.surface_scores (spaCy segmentation), not textstat's own -- the paper's call reproduces the defect that inverted Cochrane's FKGL delta
syllables_ratio via vowel-group counting, not pyphen
infrequent_words_ratio via wordfreq zero-frequency, not nltk.corpus.words membership
past_tense_verbs/past_perfect_verbs via spaCy tag_, not nltk.pos_tag
sentences_number/short_sentences_ratio via spaCy segmentation, not nltk.sent_tokenize
punctuation_ratio uses one tokenizer for both halves of the ratio; the paper mixes spaCy is_punct with an NLTK total
params.unbounded_ratios: past_tense_verbs and passive_voice_ratio can exceed 1.0. Both are reproduced as written: the numerators count VBD/VBN tags and passive *sentences* respectively, while both denominators count only pos==VERB tokens, which excludes auxiliaries. A source with 'had written' and 'was praised' scores 1.75.
params.words_per_sentence_caveat: reproduced as written -- mean(tokens per sentence) / clean tokens, which is ~1/n_sentences and not mean sentence length. M1's mean_src_sent_len is the uncorrupted quantity.

notes: Neither metric is independent evidence of meaning preservation: BLEU is in the same n-gram-overlap family as M2's ROUGE recall, and BERTScore is in the same embedding-similarity family as M4's target groundedness. Read them alongside those, not as a second opinion.
BLEU is corpus-level and has no confidence interval; averaging sentence BLEU would be a different and noisier quantity.
3 of the paper's 5 metrics are cross-lingual or French-only and are structurally undefined here; see params.

BERTScore truncation: 10 of 250 sources exceed 512 tokens, so for those pairs the score compares the target against the *opening* of the source, not the whole document. On a corpus of 6,000-token articles this makes bertscore_f1 a measure of the abstract, not the article; read it with n and this count, or not at all.

deviations_from_paper: BLEU via sacrebleu with an explicit 13a tokenizer; the paper uses easse.bleu, which is unmaintained and does not expose its tokenisation

not_applicable.camembert_score_french: French monolingual similarity; this pipeline is English-only (get_processor refuses other languages).
not_applicable.simplification_mbert_en: cross-lingual mBERT F1 between an English target and a French source; no French side exists in any corpus here.
not_applicable.simplification_mbert_fr: cross-lingual mBERT F1 between a French target and an English source; no French side exists in any corpus here.

params.headline: share_attributable_corpus = sum(attributable) / sum(total)
params.why: share_attributable is a per-pair ratio whose denominator is near zero whenever a pair changed little, so its mean is dominated by those pairs -- one contributed 6.39 of a reported corpus mean of 6.87. Read share_attributable_corpus, or the per-pair median.
